lines: The apartment rents for 900 dollars a month. But to move in, you pay the first month, a 900 dollar security deposit, and a 50 dollar application fee. That's 1,850 dollars before your first night.
How much rent can you afford? The 30 percent rule says keep rent at or below 30 percent of your income before taxes. On 3,000 dollars a month, that's 900.
Landlords have their own check. Many want your income to be at least 3 times the rent. 3 times 900 is 2,700, and you earn 3,000, so you pass.
Rent is only the start. Add utilities and renters insurance. 900 in rent, plus 110 for utilities, plus 15 for insurance, is 1,025 dollars a month.
The lease is a contract. Check how long it lasts, when rent is due, the grace period and the late fee, and what it costs to break it early.
Roommates cut the rent. A 1,400 dollar two-bedroom split two ways is 700 each. But on a shared lease, if your roommate leaves, the landlord can ask you for the whole 1,400.
On move-in day, take dated photos of every scratch and stain. When you leave, the landlord can charge for damage, but not for normal wear and tear like faded paint.
A hermit crab lives in a borrowed shell, picks one that fits its body now, and moves when it outgrows it. Pick the place that fits your income today.
